passage:
"Give me my phone," hissed Parveen. "That stranger called my drawing garbage. I'm writing something back that will make him cry."

"Wait." Her older brother Ujjwal held out his hand. "Show me what you wrote."

She showed him the draft.

"That's savage. Which is exactly what he wants, right? Something to screenshot."

"So I just let him win?"

"What happens if you don't answer?"

"He gets bored, maybe."

"Mute him. Sleep. Look at it in the morning."

Parveen sighed, muted the account and put her phone on the shelf. The next morning she read her draft once and wrinkled her nose. "Glad that never went out."

qa.q: What did the stranger call Parveen's drawing?
What was Parveen feeling about the stranger's comment, and what did she want to do?
qa.a: She felt angry and insulted, and she wanted to make him cry with a sharp reply.

qa.q: What steps helped Parveen in the end?
qa.a: She did not reply, muted the account, went to sleep and read her draft again in the morning.

qa.q: Why might the stranger want a reply from Parveen?
qa.a: Ujjwal points out he is likely after something to screenshot, so an angry reply would give him exactly what he wants.

grounding: An online stranger baits a teen into a heated reply; she learns to mute, not feed the troll, and sleep before answering.

passage: I'm Manjula, and two weeks ago I got into a pointless fight with a stranger online. I'd posted my drawing of a heron on an art forum. Someone called "realart_only" commented: "Kids shouldn't post trash. Delete this." My face went hot. At midnight I typed three long replies, each ruder than the last. The stranger kept going, and the more I answered, the more they laughed. I couldn't sleep. Next morning my friend Sabina looked at my phone and said, "You're feeding them. They want you angry." She showed me how to mute and block. I did both, and then I tried something new: I waited a whole day before posting anything. My next heron got twelve kind comments. I read them after a good night's sleep.

qa.q: What did "realart_only" comment on the heron drawing?
qa.a: The comment said, "Kids shouldn't post trash. Delete this."

qa.q: What was Manjula feeling while typing the midnight replies?
qa.a: Manjula felt hurt and angry, with a hot face, and got more heated with each reply.

qa.q: Which steps helped Manjula, and why?
qa.a: Muting and blocking cut off the troll, and waiting a day before posting stopped Manjula reacting in anger.

qa.q: How did the stranger likely see Manjula's angry replies?
qa.a: The stranger probably enjoyed them, since the more Manjula answered, the more they laughed.

grounding: Illustrates a teen baited by an online stranger into heated replies, then learning not to feed trolls, to mute and block, and to sleep first.

passage:
Warden's log, boys' hostel, Tuesday night (Preeti, night warden)
12:40 a.m. On my round I found Hrithik, Class 11, sitting up under his blanket, phone glowing, jaw clenched. He said a stranger on a cricket forum had called his home state "full of idiots" and he was "destroying" them. He had sent fifteen replies. I asked him to read me the last one aloud. He stopped halfway and went red. We talked about trolls wanting a reaction. He muted the thread, blocked the account, and agreed to leave any reply until after breakfast. Lights off at 1:05.
At breakfast he said he no longer wanted to reply at all. I will raise online baiting at Friday's house meeting.

qa.q: How many replies had Hrithik sent?
What does Hrithik going red while reading his reply aloud suggest?
qa.a: It suggests Hrithik felt embarrassed, hearing how angry and harsh the reply sounded outside his head.

qa.q: What did Preeti help Hrithik do?
qa.a: Preeti helped him see that trolls want a reaction; then he muted the thread, blocked the account and waited until after breakfast.

qa.q: How might the online stranger have felt reading fifteen replies?
qa.a: The stranger likely felt pleased, since getting Hrithik angry was the point of the insult.

grounding: Shows a teen baited by an online stranger late at night, and a warden helping him mute, block and sleep before responding.
